name: J02 — input, paste, Unicode, resize, scrolling and interruption
about: Terminal interaction against the SHIPPED binary under a real ConPTY.
Every step here is a real browser keyboard or paste event through xterm's
own encoder and paste handling - not an invocation of a product test hook -
so what it exercises is the same path a user's terminal takes.
THE PLATFORM CAVEAT THIS SCENARIO USED TO CARRY IS NOW FIXED, and the
steps below ASSERT the behaviour rather than merely recording what the
platform happened to deliver.
What it said: crossterm 0.29 has no Event::Paste on Windows at all, so
ConPTY delivered every pasted newline as a key record indistinguishable
from Enter and the multiline paste SUBMITTED its earlier lines instead of
composing them, while U+2014 and U+2211 were dropped before reaching the
client. The evidence for that is preserved in the j02-double run, whose
transcript holds `[text] echo line one` and `[text] echo   line two` as two
sent turns with only `line three` left in the composer.
What changed: on Windows the client now sets ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT
through a safe console-mode wrapper and owns the stdin byte reader itself,
parsing the bracketed-paste framing rather than consuming crossterm's
translated key events — which drop the escape introducer and lose those
characters. Measured, not assumed; see crates/grapt-client/src/vt.rs.
So the multiline paste below must COMPOSE, leaving the transcript empty,
and the non-ASCII text must arrive intact. Both are asserted.

steps.paste:
line one
	line two indented by a real tab
line three

steps.capture: a multiline paste, composed rather than submitted
non-ASCII text, which the byte reader keeps intact
